name: LM4050BEX3-5.0+T
title: LM4050/LM4051 50ppm/°C precision micropower shunt voltage references, 1.225 V to 5.000 V
summary: Two-terminal bandgap shunt references that hold a fixed reverse breakdown voltage, like a precise zener, at any reverse current from about 60 µA to 15 mA. The LM4051 is the 1.225 V version; the LM4050 comes in 2.048, 2.500, 3.000, 3.3, 4.096 and 5.000 V. Each voltage is sold in three initial-accuracy grades (A 0.1%, B 0.2%, C 0.5%) with a 50 ppm/°C maximum temperature coefficient over -40°C to +125°C, in 3-pin SC70 or SOT23. No output capacitor is needed and any capacitive load is stable. LM4050BEX3-5.0+T is the 5.000 V, B-grade (0.2%) part in SC70, marked ASZ.
key_figures: ±50 ppm/°C max at IR = 1 mA; ±15 ppm/°C typ at 100 µA
60 µA to 15 mA (IRMIN max 60 µA to 80 µA by voltage)
20 µVRMS (1.225 V) to 80 µVRMS (5.000 V), 10 Hz to 10 kHz

notes: The letter after LM4050 or LM4051 is the accuracy grade; EM3 is SOT23 and EX3 is SC70; the suffix after the dash names the voltage.
Parts with /V in the number are the AEC-Q100 qualified versions.
LM4050AEX3-2.5/V+T, LM4050AEX3-3.3/V+T and LM4050CEX3-3.3/V+T all carry the top mark +AUE.

circuits.title: Typical operating circuit
circuits.description: A resistor RS from the supply VS feeds the cathode (+) of the shunt reference, whose anode (-) is grounded. The reference sinks whatever part of the resistor current the load does not take, holding VR at its breakdown voltage; the resistor carries ISHUNT + ILOAD. RS is chosen from the equations for the supply range and the load range.
notes: The load connects between VR and ground and draws ILOAD.

circuits.title: Load-transient test circuit
circuits.description: A DC source VB biases the reference through 1 kΩ. A square-wave generator VGEN, returned to ground, steps the current drawn from the VR node through RL; the change in VR is watched AC-coupled. RL is 100 kΩ, 10 kΩ or 1 kΩ for the ±25 µA, ±250 µA and ±2.5 mA steps.

circuits.title: Startup characteristics test circuit
circuits.description: A pulse source VIN, 1 Hz with 50% duty cycle, drives the reference through RS; VR is measured across the reference. RS is 30 kΩ for the 2.5 V part and 16 kΩ for the 5.0 V part.

equations.name: Bias resistor range
equations.note: The upper bound keeps at least 60 µA through the reference at the lowest supply and the heaviest load; the lower bound keeps the shunt current under the 20 mA damage limit at the highest supply and the lightest load.

operation.text: The part uses a bandgap reference and internal pass transistors that sink current to hold a fixed voltage across its terminals, like an ideal zener, for reverse currents of 60 µA to 15 mA. With forward current up to 10 mA it clamps one diode drop below ground.

Size RS at the lowest supply and the highest load current so that at least 60 µA always flows in the reference; check that at the highest supply and the lightest load the shunt current stays under 15 mA for regulation, and never above 20 mA. Allow for the resistor's tolerance, and rate its power from PDR.
No capacitor is needed for stability, and the part is stable with any capacitance on its output.
The output temperature coefficient is typically within ±15 ppm/°C. Its sign varies from unit to unit: some parts drift up with temperature and others down.

The junction limit is +150°C and the E-grade operating limit +125°C. At 15 mA and 5 V the part dissipates 75 mW; with the SC70's 2.17 mW/°C derating above +70°C that is a 35.56°C rise, so at +125°C ambient the junction reaches 159.56°C, over the limit. At high ambient, reduce either the load or the ambient so the junction stays inside the absolute maximum ratings.
